title: No quantitative bias rates: discretization and truncation bias only qualitative

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Lemma `lem:disc` (qualitative $B_{\rm disc}\to0$), Remark `rem:rate`, Lemma `lem:trunc`, and the tuning prescription Step 1-2.

**Problem requirement:** "quantifiable error (bias and variance)" and "rigorous error bounds ... for the whole class."

**Gap A (discretization).** For the admissible class, regular variation is at INFINITY (index $\alpha\in(0,2)$); the behavior of $\sigma^2$ near $0$ is unconstrained beyond continuity ($\sigma^2(t)\to0$). Remark `rem:rate` provides a rate $B_{\rm disc}=O(\sigma(\delta)\sqrt{\log(T/\delta)})$ ONLY under local power-law self-similarity ($\sigma^2(t)\asymp t^\alpha$ near 0, e.g. fBm). For the general class Lemma `lem:disc` gives only $B_{\rm disc}\to0$ (no rate). Hence "quantifiable bias" is met only qualitatively, and the tuning step "choose $\delta$ so $|B_{\rm disc}|\le\varepsilon/3$" is not effective (cannot bound $\delta(\varepsilon)$).

**Gap B (truncation).** Lemma `lem:trunc` "proves" $B_{\rm trunc}=H_\eta(T)/T-H_\eta\to0$ by merely restating the given limit (eq. `Hdef`). No rate is established. Consequently tuning Step 1 ("choose $T$ so $|B_{\rm trunc}|\le\varepsilon/3$") cannot produce an explicit $T(\varepsilon)$; the plateau/Richardson diagnostic is purely heuristic and not backed by a proven monotonicity-with-rate statement.

**What is needed.** (i) A quantitative truncation rate, e.g. $H_\eta(T)/T-H_\eta=O(1/T)$ via Kingman subadditivity for $\log$ of the sojourn functional + regular variation, OR an honest statement that only qualitative convergence is available with the diagnostic flagged as heuristic. (ii) For discretization, either an explicit rate under a stated local-regularity hypothesis (separate theorem), or an honest "qualitative only for the general class" statement faithful to what the class guarantees.
